import matplotlib

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

PAIR_KEYS = ["0v1", "1v2", "2v3", "3v4", "4v5"]
X_LABELS = ["0 vs 1", "1 vs 2", "2 vs 3", "3 vs 4", "4 vs 5"]
x = np.arange(len(PAIR_KEYS))

MODELS = {
    "mvp_001_qwen_rewrite": {"label": "Qwen-1.5B-RW", "color": "#4e79a7", "marker": "o"},
    "exp_001_pythia":       {"label": "Pythia-1.4B",   "color": "#e15759", "marker": "s"},
    "exp_002_olmo":         {"label": "OLMo-1B",       "color": "#59a14f", "marker": "^"},
    "exp_017_qwen_cont":    {"label": "Qwen-1.5B-cont","color": "#b07aa1", "marker": "D"},
}

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
data_path = root / "artifacts" / "bootstrap_ci_4model.json"
with open(data_path) as f:
    raw = json.load(f)

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "font.size": 9,
    "axes.linewidth": 0.8,
    "xtick.major.width": 0.6,
    "ytick.major.width": 0.6,
    "xtick.direction": "in",
    "ytick.direction": "in",
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.0, 3.5), constrained_layout=True)

for key, style in MODELS.items():
    d = raw[key]
    means = [d[p]["mean_auc"] for p in PAIR_KEYS]
    ci_lo = [d[p]["ci_lower"] for p in PAIR_KEYS]
    ci_hi = [d[p]["ci_upper"] for p in PAIR_KEYS]

    ax.plot(x, means, f"-{style['marker']}", color=style["color"],
            lw=1.5, ms=5, label=style["label"], zorder=3)
    ax.fill_between(x, ci_lo, ci_hi, color=style["color"], alpha=0.15, zorder=2)

ax.axhline(y=0.60, color="gray", ls="--", lw=0.8, alpha=0.7, zorder=1)

ax.axhline(y=0.50, color="lightgray", ls=":", lw=0.6, alpha=0.7, zorder=1)

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(X_LABELS)
ax.set_xlabel("Depth Pair")
ax.set_ylabel("Pairwise AUC")
ax.set_ylim(0.45, 1.02)
ax.set_xlim(-0.15, 4.35)

ax.legend(fontsize=7.5, loc="upper right", framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="0.8")

out_dir = root / "docs" / "paper" / "figures"
out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

pdf_path = out_dir / "fig_s1_auc_decay_ci.pdf"
png_path = out_dir / "fig_s1_auc_decay_ci.png"
fig.savefig(pdf_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
fig.savefig(png_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

print(f"PDF: {pdf_path} ({pdf_path.stat().st_size / 1024:.1f} KB)")
print(f"PNG: {png_path} ({png_path.stat().st_size / 1024:.1f} KB)")
for key, style in MODELS.items():

Generative Depth Estimation Pipeline

This paper introduces a pipeline for measuring how many times a piece of text has been recursively generated by a language model (its "generational depth").

Stage 1 — Seed Text Collection:
Human-written seed documents are sampled from a source corpus (e.g., C4 web text, arXiv abstracts, Wikipedia). Each seed is 256 tokens.

Stage 2 — Recursive Generation (Depth Chain):
A generation operator G_δ (an LLM with fixed decoding parameters δ) takes the seed text X and recursively generates: X → Y_1 → Y_2 → ... → Y_K. Each output becomes the prompt for the next generation. This produces texts at depths 0 (human), 1, 2, ..., K. A curved feedback arrow loops from the output back to the input of the generator.

Stage 3 — 15-Dimensional Feature Extraction:
For each text (at any depth), 15 statistical features are computed using a fixed reference scorer (a separate small LM). The features fall into four groups:
- Surprisal statistics (mean, std, skew, kurtosis, IQR of token-level surprisal)
- Surprisal derivatives (mean/std of first differences)
- Vocabulary diversity (type-token ratio, hapax ratio, top-10/top-50 frequency mass)
- Frequency tail metrics (zipf coefficient, self-BLEU)

Stage 4 — OBD-LightGBM Classification:
An Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) classifier decomposes the ordinal depth prediction into K binary sub-problems: P(depth > k) for k = 0, 1, ..., K-1. Each sub-problem uses a LightGBM classifier on the 15D feature vector.

Stage 5 — Output:
The classifier outputs a predicted depth d-hat for each text, and the system identifies K*_empirical: the maximum depth at which adjacent generations remain statistically distinguishable (pairwise AUC > threshold θ = 0.60).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate Figure 1: Generational depth estimation pipeline diagram."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, FancyArrowPatch
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "mathtext.fontset": "cm",
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12.5, 3.2))
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 13.0)
ax.set_ylim(-0.6, 3.0)
ax.axis("off")

COLORS = {
    "seed":    ("#c5d5e4", "#3b5b7a"),
    "gen":     ("#f5e6c4", "#7a6530"),
    "feat":    ("#d4e8d0", "#3a6b35"),
    "obd":     ("#ddd0e6", "#5b3a7a"),
    "output":  ("#f2d5cb", "#7a4030"),
}

BOX_W = 2.15
BOX_H = 2.55
BOX_Y = 0.0
GAP = 0.55

boxes = [
    {"x": 0.0,                       "key": "seed",   "title": "Seed Text",
     "lines": ["(C4 / arXiv / Wiki)", "256 tokens"]},
    {"x": BOX_W + GAP,               "key": "gen",    "title": "Recursive\nGeneration",
     "lines": [r"$G_\delta = \mathrm{LLM} + \delta$", r"$X \!\to\! Y_1 \!\to\! \cdots \!\to\! Y_K$"]},
    {"x": 2*(BOX_W + GAP),           "key": "feat",   "title": "15D Feature\nExtraction",
     "lines": ["· Surprisal moments", "· Surprisal derivatives",

    {"x": 3*(BOX_W + GAP),           "key": "obd",    "title": "OBD\nLightGBM",
     "lines": [r"$K$ binary classifiers", r"$P(\mathrm{depth} > k)$"]},
    {"x": 4*(BOX_W + GAP),           "key": "output", "title": "Output",
     "lines": [r"Depth $\hat{d}$", r"$K^*_{\mathrm{empirical}}$"]},
]

    shadow = FancyBboxPatch(

        boxstyle="round,pad=0.12", facecolor=SHADOW_COLOR,

                color=fg, zorder=3)

    body_top = title_y - len(title_lines) * 0.32 - 0.15
    for j, line in enumerate(b["lines"]):

print(f"PNG: {out_dir / 'pipeline.png'}")

Generative Depth Estimation Pipeline

This paper introduces a pipeline for measuring how many times a piece of text has been recursively generated by a language model (its "generational depth").

Stage 1 — Seed Text Collection:
Human-written seed documents are sampled from a source corpus (e.g., C4 web text, arXiv abstracts, Wikipedia). Each seed is 256 tokens.

Stage 2 — Recursive Generation (Depth Chain):
A generation operator G_δ (an LLM with fixed decoding parameters δ) takes the seed text X and recursively generates: X → Y_1 → Y_2 → ... → Y_K. Each output becomes the prompt for the next generation. This produces texts at depths 0 (human), 1, 2, ..., K. A curved feedback arrow loops from the output back to the input of the generator.

Stage 3 — 15-Dimensional Feature Extraction:
For each text (at any depth), 15 statistical features are computed using a fixed reference scorer (a separate small LM). The features fall into four groups:
- Surprisal statistics (mean, std, skew, kurtosis, IQR of token-level surprisal)
- Surprisal derivatives (mean/std of first differences)
- Vocabulary diversity (type-token ratio, hapax ratio, top-10/top-50 frequency mass)
- Frequency tail metrics (zipf coefficient, self-BLEU)

Stage 4 — OBD-LightGBM Classification:
An Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) classifier decomposes the ordinal depth prediction into K binary sub-problems: P(depth > k) for k = 0, 1, ..., K-1. Each sub-problem uses a LightGBM classifier on the 15D feature vector.

Stage 5 — Output:
The classifier outputs a predicted depth d-hat for each text, and the system identifies K*_empirical: the maximum depth at which adjacent generations remain statistically distinguishable (pairwise AUC > threshold θ = 0.60).

x = np.arange(len(PAIR_KEYS))

    "mvp_001_qwen_rewrite": {"label": "Qwen-1.5B-RW", "color": "#4e79a7", "marker": "o"},

}

    raw = json.load(f)

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",

    "xtick.major.width": 0.6,

    "xtick.direction": "in",
    "ytick.direction": "in",
})

    ax.plot(x, means, f"-{style['marker']}", color=style["color"],

    ax.fill_between(x, ci_lo, ci_hi, color=style["color"], alpha=0.15, zorder=2)
